frontier.hypothesis: Target's register+displacement shape can be reached legally if some pseudo set to `(plus (reg eda) 1100)` survives delete_dead_from_cse for an HONEST reason - i.e. it is referenced elsewhere in the function because a programmer genuinely needed it there, not because it was reused to steer cse.
frontier.mechanism: delete_dead_from_cse deletes a set only when the destination pseudo's whole-function reference count is zero (cse.c:8731-8734). Any second genuine reference - a later reassignment that is really used, or a use of the pointer as a value rather than as an address - keeps the count non-zero, so the set survives into cse2 and the cheap register+displacement address is retained at all three sites.
frontier.next_probe: The +0x44C halfword is read AGAIN later in the same function: `if (((u8 *)D_800A3878)[3] & 0x2) a0_arg = D_80102326;` and D_80102326 == &eda[0x226]. Enumerate honest C shapes in which one pointer genuinely serves both that later read and the block's save/restore. The obstacle is liveness: a pointer assigned only inside `if (qf & 0x30)` and read afterwards is undefined behaviour (that is why permuter output-200-1 was rejected), so measure the function-scope variant that assigns it unconditionally BEFORE the block, and read the `la` position in the normalized diff before scoring. Note K4 (two independent pointers, ALL accesses at offset 0) measured 17, but that is a different shape from one base plus one derived pointer both genuinely used.

frontier.hypothesis: If no honest second-reference form exists, the cheapest known LEGAL closure of region A is session-3's if/ELSE diamond, and the remaining work is buying back the two placements it costs.
frontier.mechanism: An if/ELSE arm ends in an unconditional jump + BARRIER, so cse_end_of_basic_block (cse.c:8039-8184) cannot AROUND-extend past the join label and the base pseudo enters the next block with no qty_const - the fold cannot fire in cse2 regardless of what delete_dead_from_cse did.
frontier.next_probe: Re-open rejected/cse-boundary-diamond-closes-region-a-but-moves-magic-and-la.c (measured 11 with build_insns 185 == target 185 and target's exact region-A bytes). Its whole residual is two placement clusters: `magic = 0x80190800` sinks out of the prologue into the else arm (~7) and the `la` moves from inside the `qf & 0x30` block to mine[38..39] (~4). Attack the placements, not region A - e.g. find a spelling of the 0x80 test that yields the boundary while leaving `magic`'s initialisation unconditional at the top.

frontier.hypothesis: Orthogonal and byte-neutral: our prototype for func_8003AFFC is wrong and src/code6cac_c2.c carries duplicate declarations of it.
frontier.mechanism: m2c infers `func_8003AFFC(D_800A3878)` - $a0 holds the object pointer live from tgt[48] through the jal at tgt[68] with no reload - while our C calls it with no arguments.
frontier.next_probe: Read asm/funcs/func_8003AFFC.s to see whether it consumes $a0; if it does, reconcile the three duplicate `extern void func_8003AFFC(void);` declarations (src/code6cac_c2.c lines 73, 74, 171) to one correct prototype and re-measure. Expect byte-neutrality here; the value is correctness of the decompilation and of func_8003AFFC's own future grind.
